report:
## Conclusion

**Yes — corticosteroids such as dexamethasone improve survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients, but only in those with severe or critical disease requiring oxygen or ventilatory support.** The evidence is strong and consistent across multiple high-quality studies.

### Key Evidence

**1. The RECOVERY Trial (NEJM, July 2020):** This large, randomized, open-label trial assigned 2,104 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to receive dexamethasone (6 mg daily for up to 10 days) versus 4,321 patients to usual care. Dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality by 17% overall, with the greatest benefit among patients on invasive mechanical ventilation (~one-third reduction in death). Notably, **no benefit was observed in patients who did not require oxygen**, suggesting the drug should not be used in mild cases.

**2. WHO REACT Prospective Meta-Analysis (JAMA, September 2020):** The WHO Rapid Evidence Appraisal group pooled data from seven randomized trials and found that systemic corticosteroids were associated with significantly lower 28-day all-cause mortality among critically ill COVID-19 patients, confirming the RECOVERY findings across multiple settings.

**3. WHO Clinical Guidance:** Based on this evidence, the WHO issued a strong recommendation for systemic corticosteroids (e.g., dexamethasone or hydrocortisone) in patients with severe and critical COVID-19, while advising against their use in non-severe cases due to potential harm from immunosuppression.

### Important Caveat
Dexamethasone is not a blanket treatment for all COVID-19 patients. It benefits those who are severely ill with hypoxia or on ventilation. In patients with mild disease not requiring respiratory support, corticosteroids showed no benefit and may be harmful by weakening innate immunity.

### Sources
- RECOVERY Trial results (NEJM): https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436
- RECOVERY Trial press release: https://www.recoverytrial.net/news/low-cost-dexamethasone-reduces-death-by-up-to-one-third-in-hospitalised-patients-with-severe-respiratory-complications-of-covid-19
- WHO REACT Meta-Analysis (JAMA): https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279
- WHO Corticosteroids for COVID-19 Guidance: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/WHO-2019-nCoV-Corticosteroids-2020.1
